# Task map

Each task a reader wants to do with snapy is listed here once, under what the book says about it: answered,
partly documented, undocumented, unsupported by the code, or outside the scope of this report. An answered or
partly documented task names the section that answers it; a partly documented answer leaves part of the task
open, and that section says which part. A task the book does not answer gives the reason instead.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Find the section that answers a "How do I ...?" task, or why the book does not.

**Data.** `tools/reader-tasks.md`: one row per task, seeded from the newcomer question bank, tasks
readers could not find, the extension blocks and the DO cards, with the answering section or a reason.

**Placement.** Report preparation, outside the solver.

**Activation.** Run `gen_reader_tasks.py`; no solver switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Every row names a labelled section or a reason; a status records the lookup grade, not a
code audit. Three tasks still point at the verification chapter as a whole, because the section that answers
them has no label.

**Evidence.** `tools/tests/test_reader_tasks.py` fails on a section that does not exist, on a chapter target and
on a missing reason; the rendered gate checks every destination in the PDF build.
:::
